notes:
Summary: Lost at procurement to internal cloud consolidation decision — team elected AWS SageMaker managed endpoints. Key themes: ops consolidation, existing AWS discounts, and loss of internal champion.

Deal history (short): POC run Jan 2026 against recommendations / personalization workload. Redwood Dedicated configuration proposed (VPC + KMS). POC results: latency and quality comparable; Redwood had cost upside with batching suggestions but buyer prioritized single-vendor ops.

Security/Compliance: Security completed questionnaire, wanted SOC2 + KMS + audit logs. Redwood met requirements in eval but procurement favored managed endpoints for perceived simpler compliance with AWS Control Tower and existing security posture. Quote from CISO: "We prefer to keep inference inside the AWS boundary to reduce blast radius and centralize key management."

Champion situation: Lead ML platform engineer (Tom Reyes) promoted out of team during procurement window (Feb). No clear successor willing to own third-party runtime; platform team defaulted to internal managed service.

Commercial: Procurement received a negotiated AWS discount tied to existing compute commit; final numbers made Redwood Dedicated less competitive on TCO despite technical fit. Finance also flagged additional integration budget as blocker.

Next actions: closed-won improbable. Close opportunity in CRM, set 6-month winback cadence, offer to run a cost comparsion + joint benchmark with AWS to highlight unit economics.

Stadium/ambience: Shorthand notes scattered in threads: "lost to AWS — champion left", "discounts killed us", "security happy but prefer vendor consolidation".

Attachments: Fireflies call id ff_2026-01-18_SKY-POC-01 (POC walkthrough), drive pricing deck (proposal v2), security Q&A doc.

Internal feedback to AE/SE: avoid multi-cloud discount mismatch next cycle; push winback play around unique fallback/routing capabilities and Optimize tooling that can show immediate cost delta.
